newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Tele Danmark says to cut 2,000 staff.
newsitem.headline: Danish Tele Danmark says to cut 2,000 staff.

text.p: Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark on Wednesday announced a streamlining programme including a net staff reduction of 2,000 people by mid-1998.
Other changes would include welding seven currently separate divisions into one and putting internet operations into a specialist unit.
"The company's board has undertaken a reorganisation in order to strengthen the group's position in an increasingly competitive market," it said.

"Ongoing evaluation of improvement and rationalisation projects show possibilities to let about 2,500 workers go before the middle of 1998. One should reckon on external recruitment of around 500 new staff during the same period, giving a net reduction of 2,000," it added.
The dismissals would entail extra costs but these should swiftly be covered by wage savings.
Tele Denmark's share was barely moved, slipping one crown to 354 crowns.

In a move seen as perhaps as a further step toward full privatisation, the state run former monopoly on Tuesday said that it was buying back privately held A-shares in order to phase them out and simplify its equity structure by June 1998.
The manoeuvre slightly raises the state's share of the company, partially privatised in 1994, to 51.73 percent from 51.00 percent.

The government, which pledged to balance the public-sector budget and reduce foreign debt, has said that it does not see itself retaining control of the group indefinitely but would not sell any shares in 1997.

It does not say when a further selloff is likely although 1998 -- as well as seeing the share rationalisation and the culmination of the staff reduction plan -- is also scheduled to be an election year.
